headline: High: Aci’s broad egress plus Plandex’s filesystem/git write path creates default-risk leakage, conflict, and cascading-action hazards.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aci can ingest and emit CRM/email/calendar content through APIs, and Plandex reads/writes project files and stdin/stdout. If Aci’s outputs are copied into Plandex plans or files, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream instructions. The shared bridge is indirect, but the pathway exists in common workflows.
conditions: IF Aci output is pasted or written into a Plandex plan/file, injection is possible.
IF Plandex treats imported text as instructions without provenance checks, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Use a strict prompt delimiter for any copied Aci output.
Review imported text before Plandex execution.
Disable auto-apply for plans containing external text.
Keep Aci outputs in read-only notes, not executable plan files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aci touches CRM, email, customer support, and calendar data, while Plandex has broad network egress and can read/write local files. If shared workspaces or copied artifacts contain sensitive records, Plandex may transmit them to its model provider or Plandex Cloud. That creates a default exfiltration path with meaningful blast radius.
conditions: IF Aci-derived files or transcripts are placed in Plandex’s project directory, leakage is possible.
IF Plandex sends file contents to a third-party model provider or cloud backend, sensitive data can leave the workspace.
mitigations: Keep CRM/email exports out of Plandex workspaces.
Redact PII before any handoff.
Use a local-only model/provider configuration if available.
Restrict Plandex to synthetic or scrubbed examples.
Audit outbound requests for sensitive payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aci can make direct API calls and handle OAuth/secrets, while Plandex can execute shell, modify git state, and write files. Both support multiple instances, and Plandex shares state via a backend. Concurrent edits to the same repo or integration targets can race and overwrite each other, especially without explicit locking.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or workspace, write conflicts can occur.
IF Aci and Plandex act on the same external API account, overlapping mutations can race.
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories or accounts.
Serialize writes with a manual lock file.
Disable one agent’s write access during the other’s run.
Review git diffs before apply.
Use separate OAuth principals for each agent.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions, and Plandex can execute shell and modify git state. If Plandex consumes Aci-produced facts or drafts without verification, a mistaken or injected Aci output can cascade into irreversible commits, emails, or API actions. The pair’s default toolchain makes downstream action-taking plausible.
conditions: IF Plandex uses Aci output as authoritative input, cascading error is possible.
IF Plandex auto-applies changes derived from Aci-generated content, downstream harm can occur.
mitigations: Require human review before apply.
Cross-check Aci outputs against source systems.
Disable auto-apply for any Aci-derived plan.
Log provenance for each imported fact.
Limit Aci-to-Plandex handoffs to summaries, not commands.

E_compliance.rationale: Aci touches customer support, CRM, email, and calendar data, while Plandex handles source code and can transmit file contents to a model provider or cloud backend. If regulated customer data is mixed into code workspaces, retention and residency policies can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific residency breach, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is placed into Plandex-managed files, compliance mismatch risk increases.
IF Plandex cloud/model-provider retention differs from Aci’s data handling, policy divergence occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of code workspaces.
Use separate retention policies per system.
Document data-flow boundaries.
Prefer self-hosted/local inference where possible.
Review vendor DPAs and residency settings.
